definition: Implied, understood, or inferred without being explicitly stated in text or protocol manuals.
etymology: From French tacite, from Latin tacitus ('silent').
manuscriptExample: The manuscript relies on the tacit assumption that cell density remains constant throughout the 72-hour readout.
conferenceExample: There was tacit consensus among peer reviewers that the manuscript merits a major revision.

definition: Relating to the complete set of RNA transcripts produced by the genome under specific physiological conditions.
manuscriptExample: Transcriptomic profiling identified 142 differentially expressed genes involved in cholesterol biosynthesis.
conferenceExample: The reviewer commended the inclusion of bulk and single-cell transcriptomic validation cohorts.

definition: Lasting only for a short time; impermanent or non-integrated gene expression or physiological event.
etymology: From Latin transiens, present participle of transire ('to pass over').
manuscriptExample: Transient plasmid transfection achieved peak luciferase expression at 24 hours post-lipofection.
conferenceExample: We addressed whether the calcium flux represented a transient spike or sustained cytosolic elevation.

definition: Relating to the application of basic scientific discoveries into clinical therapies or medical practice.
manuscriptExample: The manuscript highlights the translational significance of targeting mutant allele X in patient-derived models.
conferenceExample: The associate editor praised the study for bridging basic mechanistic insights and clinical translational potential.
